title: When the Appraisal Ordering Clock Starts for Rate Lock Commitment Extension Disputes
content:
In a **Rate Lock Commitment** dispute against an extension charge, the appraisal ordering days are counted in calendar days from the clock start to the date the appraisal order was placed. The clock start depends on the file's **Appraisal Order** (why the order exists, and the date it was placed) and on the intent-to-proceed date on the **Mortgage Loan File**.

**Rule.** The ordering clock does not always start at the intent to proceed:

- **Transferred order.** When the appraisal order was transferred in from another lender, the clock starts on the date the order was placed, so no ordering days arise.
- **Weekend intent to proceed.** When the order was not transferred in and the borrower gave the intent to proceed on a Saturday or a Sunday, the clock starts on the following Monday, because Larkspur's appraisal desk places orders on business days.
- **Otherwise.** The clock starts on the intent-to-proceed date.

The weekday of the intent-to-proceed date is taken from the calendar, counted in whole weeks from Monday 2024-01-01.

| Order reason | Intent to proceed given on | Clock starts on | Days counted to the order date |
|---|---|---|---|
| Transferred in from another lender | Any day | The order date | 0 |
| Any other reason | Saturday | The following Monday (2 days later) | Days from that Monday |
| Any other reason | Sunday | The following Monday (1 day later) | Days from that Monday |
| Any other reason | Monday to Friday | The intent-to-proceed date | Days from that date |

### Hypothetical cases

- Intent to proceed on Saturday 4 May 2024, order placed Monday 13 May 2024 (a standard order). The clock starts Monday 6 May, so 7 days are counted.
- The same dates on a transferred-in order: 0 days are counted.
- Intent to proceed on Wednesday 8 May 2024, order placed Friday 17 May 2024: 9 days are counted.
